title: At the Doctor's / Ku mubiri w'igitero
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugena ububabare tubofasha n'ibice biranga 'me duele' + igice cy'umubiri (me duele la cabeza). Mu Icyongereza, uburyo bwo kugena bubiri: 'I have' + 'a headache' (tengo un dolor de cabeza). Ni ubugambi bwinshi kubera ko batavuga 'I hurt my head' kugena ububabare buhagije. Nanone, mu Icyongereza, 'hurt' bishobora kuba ngombwa: 'My head hurts' (mi cabeza duele). Kugira inguvu z'ikisanze 'have' n'amabwiriza yo ku bababare n'ikisanze 'hurt' n'abantu bishobora kuba byihuse kugena mu buryo burangwa.
rule: Kugena ibibababare n'indwara mu Icyongereza ku murongo A2, tubofasha n'ibintu bya 1) 'I have' + igisubizo (a headache, a cold, a fever, a cough, a sore throat, a stomachache, etc.) kugena ko unadukuye. 2) 'My [igice cy'umubiri] hurts' cyangwa 'My [igice cy'umubiri] is sore' kugena ububabare ku rugero rutandukanye. 3) 'I feel' + igisubizo (sick, dizzy, tired, etc.) kugena ibyiza by'umubiri byose. Mu ibibazo n'ibimenyetso byihuse, tubofasha n'ibice 'do/does' (Do you have...? Yes, I do. No, I don't). Kugena ibyifuzo, tubofasha n'ibice 'should' / 'shouldn't' (You should rest, You shouldn't eat spicy food). Remera ko 'hurt' ni ngombwa idakomoka: hurt - hurt - hurt. Batabofasha n'ibice 'me duele' bihagije; bashyiramo umuntu: 'My head hurts' (nta 'I hurt my head' usibye ubwo ari ububabare bw'akayira). Nanone, 'I've got' ni uburyo bw'amagambo 'I have got' (I've got a cold). Mu mibare yo mu gishushanyo, bashobora kugena 'I have a cold'.

concept_examples.text: I have a headache and a sore throat.
concept_examples.translation: Nifite ububabare bw'umutwe no kugena ububabare bw'ikinyabwoya.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˈhɛdeɪk ənd ə sɔːr θroʊt/

concept_examples.text: My stomach hurts after eating.
concept_examples.translation: Ububabare bw'ikibindi bwagira nyuma yo kurya.

concept_examples.text: Do you have a fever?
You should drink a lot of water.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd drɪŋk ə lɒt əv ˈwɔːtər/

common_error.explanation: Ibikorwa byagiye kugira ububabare bw'ubushishozwe 'me duele la cabeza' nk'uko 'I hurt my head'. Ariko 'hurt' kuba ngombwa yihuse bishobora gutanga ububabare (me lastimé la cabeza). Kugena ububabare buhagije, tubofasha n'ibice 'have a headache' cyangwa 'my head hurts'. Remera: 'hurt' kuba ngombwa idakomoka (nta igisubizo) bishobora gutanga ububabare, ariko n'umuntu igice cy'umubiri (my head hurts). Vuga ubufasha 'have' + igisubizo kugena ibyiza by'umubiri byose.

examples.original: I have a cold.
examples.note: Bofasha 'have' + ububabare cyangwa igisubizo. Ntivuge 'I am cold' kugena ububabare bw'umukandara, bishobora gutanga ko unashize.

examples.original: I have a cough and a runny nose.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə kɒf ænd ə ˈrʌni noʊz/
examples.note: Ububabare bw'ibice 'and' ni byose: cough and runny nose. Remera 'runny nose' (ikinyabwoya cyo kugena ububabare).

examples.original: I feel dizzy.
examples.note: 'Feel' + igisubizo kugena ibyiza by'umubiri. Mu gaciri tubofasha n'ibice 'me siento', ariko mu Icyongereza batabofasha n'ibice 'I feel me'.

examples.original: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Reba idava iyi kabiri ku munsi.
examples.note: Ngombwa 'take' bishobora kugenzwa n'idava, nta 'drink' (kushyura). 'Twice a day' bishobora gutanga kabiri ku munsi.

examples.original: You should rest in bed.
examples.note: Kugena ibyifuzo, 'should' + ngombwa idakomoka. Ni byihuse kurushwa 'must' (ububabare).

examples.original: I need to make an appointment.
examples.note: Bofasha 'make an appointment' kugena ububabare. 'Need to' + ngombwa bishobora gutanga ububabare.

examples.original: My back hurts a lot.
examples.note: 'A lot' ku mwishura cyangwa nyuma yo ngombwa. Ntivuge 'my back hurts much' nta 'a'.

examples.original: I have a sharp pain in my chest.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ʃɑːrp peɪn ɪn maɪ tʃɛst/
examples.note: Bofasha 'sharp' kugena ububabare bw'ikibabi n'ububabare bw'ikibabi. Shagisha ubwoko n'ibice 'in my + igice cy'umubiri'.

examples.original: My knee is swollen and red.
examples.translation: Ikiji cyange cyagiye kuba cyinshi n'ubusa.
examples.note: Bofasha 'is' + igisubizo kugena ubwoko. Remera ko 'swollen' ni igisubizo idakomoka.

title: Booking Accommodation / Gutora umugoroba
bridge: Mu gaciriyubwenge, dushtura gushtura amagambo ‘gutora’ bikorwa nyabagendwa (‘ndatora urugo’), ariko mu gaciriyubwenge, ‘would like’ + ‘to book’ ni bikorwa kugira ngo ubureze. Nanone, kugirango ubone neza iby’amagambo, mu gaciriyubwenge, dushtura ‘urugo rw’abantu babiri’ hamwe n’igitangaza nyuma, ariko mu gaciriyubwenge, igitangaza bikuye mbere (‘double room’). Nanone, mu gaciriyubwenge, dushtura ‘for’ kugirango tubyerekeze ubushake (‘for two nights’), ariko mu gaciriyubwenge, dushtura ‘por dos noches’.
rule: Kugirango utore umugoroba mu gaciriyubwenge kuri A2, shiraho gutumisha ibyago birenga: ‘Ndashaka gutora...’ (Ndashaka gutora...), ‘Ndashaka kugura umugoroba’ (Ndashaka kugura umugoroba). Ushobora gutumisha ubwoko bw’iminsi kugirango ubere imbaraga: ‘Izina ryanjye ni...’. Kuri minsi, shiraho gutumisha ‘on’ hamwe n’iminsi (‘on Monday’) na ‘for’ hamwe n’ubushake (‘for three nights’). Kuri kubuha ubushake, shiraho gutumisha ‘Mufite...?’ (Mufite...?) cyangwa ‘Hari...?’ (Hari...?). Ibyakozwe by’urugo ni: ‘urugo rw’umuntu umwe’ (urugo rw’umuntu umwe), ‘urugo rw’abantu babiri’ (urugo rw’abantu babiri), ‘urugo rw’abantu babiri’ (urugo rw’abantu babiri). Remera ko mu gaciriyubwenge, uburyo bw’amagambo ni igitangaza + igisubizo. Kuri kubuha ibikorwa, shiraho gutumisha ‘with’ (na): ‘na urubura’ (na urubura), ‘na ishuri’ (na ishuri).

concept_examples.text: I would like to book a double room for two nights.
concept_examples.translation: Ndashaka gutora urugo rw’abantu babiri por dos noches.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tə bʊk ə ˈdʌbəl ruːm fɔː tuː naɪts/

concept_examples.text: Do you have any rooms available for this weekend?
concept_examples.translation: Mufite urugo rw’umuntu umwe ubushake ku wa mbere y’icyumweru?
concept_examples.phonetic: /duː juː hæv ˈɛni ruːmz əˈveɪləbəl fɔː ðɪs ˌwiːkˈɛnd/

concept_examples.text: I'd like a room with a sea view, please.
concept_examples.translation: Ndashaka urugo na urubura rw’amajuru, yegwe.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk ə ruːm wɪð ə siː vjuː pliːz/

concept_examples.text: How much does it cost per night?
concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ mʌtʃ dʌz ɪt kɒst pɜː naɪt/

common_error.wrong: I want reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct: I would like to reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct_alt: I'd like to book a room for two nights.
common_error.explanation: Mu gaciriyubwenge, dushtura ‘ndashaka gutora’ hamwe n’igisubizo ‘gutura’, ariko mu gaciriyubwenge, ‘want’ ni bikorwa cyane kandi bishobora kuba bitangaje. Ni byo ku byerekeye, shiraho gutumisha ‘would like’ (ndashaka). Nanone, nyuma y’ ‘would like’, shiraho gutumisha ‘to’ + igisubizo mu bwoko bw’imvugo: ‘Ndashaka gutora’. Ntushobora kuba ‘Ndashaka gutora’ (bihagije ‘to’). Nanone, ushobora gutumisha ‘book’ (gutora) kuba ni bikorwa cyane mu nzu y’ubucuruzi.

examples.original: Do you have a single room available?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː hæv ə ˈsɪŋɡəl ruːm əˈveɪləbəl/
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘Do you have...?’ kubuha mu bwoko bw’iminsi. ‘Available’ bikuye nyuma y’igisubizo.

examples.original: Is there a room for tonight?
examples.translation: Hari urugo rw’umuntu umwe ku ya mbere y’icyumweru?
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘Is there...?’ kubuha ibintu byashoboye kuba.

examples.original: Are there any free rooms on Friday?
examples.phonetic: /ɑːr ðeər ˈɛni friː ruːmz ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ/
examples.translation: Hari urugo rw’umuntu umwe ubushake ku wa mbere y’icyumweru?
examples.note: Kuri ibyago byinshi, shiraho gutumisha ‘Are there any...?’. Remera ‘on’ kuri minsi y’icyumweru.

examples.original: I'm sorry, we're fully booked.
examples.note: Igisubizo kizwi cane kugirango kubuha ko nta urugo. ‘Fully booked’ bikubiyemo byose.

examples.original: I'd like to book a double room for three nights.
examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk tə bʊk ə ˈdʌbəl ruːm fɔː θriː naɪts/
examples.translation: Ndashaka gutora urugo rw’abantu babiri por tres noches.
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘I’d like’ (igikorwa cya ‘would like’) kugirango ubureze.

examples.original: Can I reserve a room with a balcony?
examples.phonetic: /kæn aɪ rɪˈzɜːv ə ruːm wɪð ə ˈbælkəni/
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘Can I...?’ kugirango ubaze ububasha. ‘With’ bikorwa kugirango ubyongeze ibintu.

examples.original: My name is Ana García. I have a reservation.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ neɪm ɪz ˈɑːnə ɡɑːrˈsiːə aɪ hæv ə ˌrezəˈveɪʃən/
examples.translation: Izina ryanjye ni Ana García. Nfite umugoroba.
examples.note: Igihe ubaga mu nzu y’ubucuruzi, shiraho kuba izina ryawe na ko ufite umugoroba. ‘Reservation’ ni igisubizo kigezwe no mu gaciriyubwenge.

examples.original: I need to cancel my reservation.
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘need to’ + igisubizo kugirango ubyerekeze ubushake. ‘Cancel’ ni kigezwe no mu gaciriyubwenge.

examples.original: How much is it per night?
examples.note: Shiraho gutumisha ‘How much’ kubuha inguvu. ‘Per night’ bikubiyemo ‘por noche’.

examples.original: Does the price include breakfast?
examples.note: Mu bwoko bw’umuntu umwe, shiraho gutumisha ‘Does’ kubuha. ‘Include’ ni kigezwe no mu gaciriyubwenge ‘incluir’.

examples.original: Is Wi-Fi free?
examples.note: Mu gaciriyubwenge, ‘is’ bikuye mbere y’umuntu mu bibazo. ‘Free’ bishobora kubikubiyemo ‘ububasha’ cyangwa ‘ububasha’.

examples.original: What time is check-out?
examples.note: Check-out ni isa cy’ubutaha, check-in ni isa cy’ububiko. Bikorwa nka magambo.

title: At the Bank or Exchange Office / Mu banka cyangwa mu nzira y'kubika icurasi
bridge: Mu gacanga, kugirango ubaze ikintu mu kugena, ubika 'I would like...' cyangwa 'Can I...?', ndetse mu ikinyarwanda dukoresha 'Nshaka...' cyangwa 'Mbega mba...?'. Uzobona ko mu gacanga amatsinda y’umwirondoro ‘can’ na ‘would’ biga bigaragara hanyuma y’itsinda ry’ishushanyo, bitagira ‘to’, n’uko iby’ingenzura nk’ ‘some’ cyangwa ‘any’ bifuza gutandukanywa kandi iby’amajuro n’ibifubisha birahishurwa mu buryo butandukanye: mu mufuzo ‘100 dollars’ ibivugwa ‘one hundred dollars’, n’amajuro y’uburemere bishimishwa na ‘point’, atagira ‘comma’.
rule: Kugirango ukore ibikorwa mu banka cyangwa mu nzira y'kubika icurasi, ubishaka kubika iby’umugeni bidasanzwe na ‘I would like’ (nshaka) bigaragara hanyuma y’izina ry’ikintu cyangwa ‘to’ + itsinda ry’ishushanyo. Mu mufuzo: ‘I would like to exchange dollars’ (Nshaka kubika ama dollars). Naho ‘Can I...?’ (Mbega naba...?) bikoreshwa kugirango ubaze ububasha, nk’uko bivugwa ‘Can I open an account?’ (Mbega naba kugura konti?). Kugirango ubaze ubwoko bw’icurasi, ubivuga ‘What is the exchange rate?’ (Ni ubuhe ubwoko bw’icurasi?). Remera ko mu gacanga amatsinda y’ubwoko n’ibindi bitagaragara bifuza ‘some’ (mu mufuzo) na ‘any’ (mu mubisha cyangwa mu ibaze). Ni by’ingenzi no kumenya uburyo amatsinda bishimishwa: mu ibaze, itsinda ry’ububasha cyangwa ry’umwirondoro birabiganira hanyuma y’itsinda ry’ishushanyo. Kugirango uvuze amajuro, ubishaka kubika amajuro y’ubwoko n’icurasi hanyuma, mu mufuzo ‘fifty dollars’ (ama dollars makumyabiri).

concept_examples.text: I would like to exchange some dollars.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tuː ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ sʌm ˈdɑːlərz/

concept_examples.text: What is the exchange rate?
Can I open a bank account?
concept_examples.translation: Mbega naba kugura konti mu banka?

concept_examples.text: I need to withdraw some money.

common_error.correct_alt: I would like to change money.
common_error.explanation: Mu ikinyarwanda duvuga ‘nshaka kubika amafaranga’ bitagira ijambo ry’ububiko, ariko mu gacanga amatsinda nk’ ‘want’ na ‘would like’ bishaka ijambo ry’ububiko ‘to’ hanyuma y’itsinda ry’ishushanyo igaragara hanyuma y’itsinda ry’ububiko. Ndetse ubwo ubishakiye ‘to’ hanyuma y’ ‘want’, ibivugwa ntibifite uburyo. Remera gusaba ‘to’ hagati y’itsinda ry’ububiko n’itsinda ry’ishushanyo.

examples.original: I would like to exchange euros for pounds.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tuː ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ ˈjʊərəʊz fɔː paʊndz/
examples.translation: Nshaka kubika ama euro mu maki.
examples.note: Bika ‘for’ kugirango uvuze icurasi ushaka kubona.

examples.original: What is the rate for dollars?
examples.translation: Ni ubuhe ubwoko bw’icurasi by’ama dollars?
examples.note: Ibaze ubwoko bw’icurasi ukoresheje ‘rate’.

examples.original: Can I have some small bills?
examples.note: ‘Small bills’ bishimisha amafaranga menshi.

examples.original: Is there a commission?
examples.note: Mu gacanga, ibaze ukoresheje ‘Is there...?’ kuri ibyo kimwe.

examples.original: I want to deposit this check into my account.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒnt tuː dɪˈpɒzɪt ðɪs tʃek ˈɪntuː maɪ əˈkaʊnt/
examples.translation: Nshaka kwinjiza cheki mu konti yange.
examples.note: Bika ‘into my account’ kugirango uvuze aho amafaranga ashaka kwinjirwa.

examples.original: Can you withdraw money from my account?
examples.phonetic: /kæn juː wɪðˈdrɔː ˈmʌni frɒm maɪ əˈkaʊnt/
examples.translation: Mbese mba kugura amafaranga mu konti yange?
examples.note: ‘Withdraw from’ ni ijambo ry’ububiko ridasanzwe.

examples.original: How much is the service fee?
examples.note: Ibaze ubushobozi ukoresheje ‘How much’.

examples.original: My account number is 12345.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ əˈkaʊnt ˈnʌmbər ɪz wʌn tuː θriː fɔː faɪv/
examples.note: Mu gacanga, amajuro ashimishwa ashushanywa cyangwa mu buryo bwinshi.

examples.original: I need to transfer money online.
examples.note: Bika ‘online’ kugirango uvuze ibikorwa by’integorwa.

examples.note: ‘Currency’ bishimisha icurasi cy’igihugu kinini.

title: Job Interview Basics / Interviyu y’akazi ya mbanza
bridge: Mu bihe bitewe n’interviyu y’akazi mu gihugu cy’Igongereza, ibibazo bitangwa neza no bikoranyijwe. Ahubwo kandi, atari nk’iki kinyarwanda, nta ‘tú’ biterwa cyangwa bitagariterwa; byose birimo ni ‘you’. Nanone, ni byaba bikorwa kubwira ubushakashatsi bwawe no kugena akazi wako wari wakoze mu gihe cyashize ubwo ugira icyo ukora.
rule: Kugira ngo ubwire neza ibintu byawe, shimira ‘I am’ (nari/nari) na ‘I have’ (nifite). Kugira ngo ubwire neza ibintu ukora, shimira ubwoko bw’imperatif: ‘I work as...’ (nkorera nka...). Kugira ngo ubwire neza akazi wako wari wakoze mu gihe cyashize, shimira ubwoko bw’imperatif: ‘I worked at...’ (nari nkorera mu...). Ibibazo byaba bikorwa ni: ‘What do you do?’ (Ukoze iki?), ‘Why do you want this job?’ (Kuki ushaka akazi k’ubwoko bwawe?), ‘What are your strengths?’ (Ni iki cyo kuba wowe?). Remera ko mu gihugu cy’Igongereza, nta n’ubwo butegetswe.

concept_examples.text: I am a student.
I have experience in customer service.
I worked at a restaurant.
Why do you want this job?

common_error.explanation: Mu kinyarwanda tusubira ‘nifite imyaka 25’, ariko mu gihugu cy’Igongereza, uburanga buvugwa n’ijambo ‘to be’ (kuba/kuba) si n’ijambo ‘have’ (kuba). Nta wigeze afata neza.

examples.original: My name is Ana.
examples.note: Shimira ‘my name is’ kugira ngo ubwire neza izina ryawe mu buryo bw’ubushishozi.

examples.original: I am from Mexico.
examples.note: Shimira ‘from’ kugira ngo ubwire neza ahantu wajyijwe.

examples.original: I live in Madrid.
examples.note: Shimira ubwoko bw’imperatif kugira ngo ubwire neza ibintu byawe byose.

examples.original: I can speak English.
examples.note: ‘Can’ buvuga ubushakashatsi, nta dusaba ‘sé’ nk’mu kinyarwanda.

examples.original: I am good at computers.
examples.note: Shimira ‘good at’ + ijambo ry’ishushanyo cyangwa ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’imperatif.

examples.original: I know how to use Excel.
examples.note: Shimira ‘know how to’ + ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’imperatif.

examples.original: What are your strengths?
examples.note: Ibibazo byaba bikorwa, wisubize n’ijambo ‘I am...’ cyangwa ‘I can...’.

examples.original: Why do you want this job?
examples.note: Shimira ‘because’ kugira ngo ubwire neza ibiranga.

examples.original: I work well in a team.
examples.note: Vuga ubushakashatsi bwawe n’amajambo yo kugenzura.

title: At the post office / Mu biro by'ibipimo
bridge: Mu gihugu cy'Angilize, kugena ubushakashatsi n'ibyo wishaka mu biro by'ibipimo, bashimira amatsinda agira ata 'I need to' cyangwa 'I'd like to', ariko mu ikinyarwanda tushema 'nashaka' cyangwa 'nahabwa'. Nanone, mu gihugu cy'Angilize, ishitsina 'send' ishishwa n'ijambo 'to' kugena aho ubicisha (send something to someone), ariko mu ikinyarwanda tushema 'guhagarika ikintu ku wundi'. Mena ubwoba ku mpamvu z'ijambo mu ibibazo nk'ibiri mu 'How much does it cost?', aho mu ikinyarwanda tusabuza 'Ni cyingeye gute?'.
rule: Kugena ibyerekeye gutuma ibintu n'ubucuruzi bw'ibipimo mu gihugu cy'Angilize ku mubare w'A2, shimira ibyo bitondetse: 1) 'I need to + ishitsina' (nahabwa + kugenzura) kugena ubushakashatsi, ntibip. 'I need to send this package.' 2) 'I'd like to + ishitsina' (nashaka + kugenzura) kugena ibyo wishaka mu buryo bw'ubwoba, ntibip. 'I'd like to buy some stamps.' 3) 'How much is/are...?' n' 'How much does it cost?' kugena amafaranga, ntibip. 'How much is the shipping?' 4) Kugena 'to' nyuma y'ishitsina nk' 'send' n' 'mail' kugena uwicishijwe, ntibip. 'Send it to my friend.' 5) Ibibazo n'ijambo 'where' n' 'when' kugena ubushakashatsi bw'ubucuruzi, ntibip. 'Where can I pick up my package?' Mena ko mu gihugu cy'Angilize, ijambo ry'igishushanyo riga burundu ry'ijambo ry'ikintu (registered mail), hataruwiki mu ikinyarwanda rirashobora kuba nyuma (ibipimo by'ububiko).

concept_examples.translation: Ubu biro by'ibipimo bufite aho nashobora kumenya aho ipakasi yanjye igiye?

common_error.correct: How much does the shipping cost?
common_error.explanation: Ibi bikorwa kubera mu ikinyarwanda tusabuza 'Ni cyingeye gute?', ariko mu gihugu cy'Angilize, ibibazo by' 'cost' birakeneye ijambo 'does' n'ishitsina mu ndangu y'ibinyacumu. Ntibishobora gushema 'costs' nyuma y' 'does'. Undi mpanuro ni kugena 'is' aho 'cost' kuriho.

examples.note: Shimira ijambo 'can' kugena ibintu byoshobora kuba.

examples.original: I want to send this box to my friend in Colombia.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɑnt tə sɛnd ðɪs bɒks tə maɪ frɛnd ɪn kəˈlɒmbiə/
examples.translation: Nashaka kuhagarika ikibande kuri mwene wanjye mu Colombia.
examples.note: Shimira 'to' kugena uwicishijwe n' 'in' kugena igihugu.

examples.original: This package is too big for the mailbox.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs ˈpækɪdʒ ɪz tuː bɪg fɔr ðə ˈmeɪlbɒks/
examples.translation: Ipakasi iyi ni cyane kurushwa mu bwadahandi.
examples.note: Shimira 'too + igishushanyo' kugena ububiko bukomeye.

examples.original: What is the delivery time to the United States?
examples.phonetic: /wʌt ɪz ðə dɪˈlɪvəri taɪm tə ðə juˈnaɪtɪd steɪts/
examples.translation: Ni ubuhe igihe cy'gutanga ku United States?
examples.note: Sabuza n'ijambo 'what' kugena ubushakashatsi bw'ibintu byose.

title: Renting a Flat / Gutegura iduha
bridge: Mu igifaransa, kugira ngo dufate neza ku gutegura iduha, tubona amazina 'gutegura' cyangwa 'kugura', kandi kugira ngo tubyivuge ko iduha irimo ubwoko, tubwira 'irimo ubwoko' cyangwa 'igitero'. Mu icyongereza, tubona 'rent' kugira ngo dufate neza ku gutegura n'ubwoko, kandi 'available' cyangwa 'for rent' kugira ngo tubyivuge ko irimo ubwoko. Nigira umutwe ku ijambo ry'imikorere: mu icyongereza tubwira 'rent an apartment' (bitagira ijambo ry'imikorere), nyamara mu igifaransa, hafi tubwira 'gutegura iduha'. Nanone, mu icyongereza, amabwiriza yihuse zeretse zeretse yigisha 'is for rent' cyangwa 'is available', ibyo mu igifaransa bivugwa n'uko 'igitero' cyangwa 'irimo ubwoko'.
rule: Kugira ngo dufate neza ku gutegura mu icyongereza ku murongo wa A2, wigeze wumenya: (1) Ijambo 'to rent' (gutegura) n'uburyo bwayo: rent / rents / renting / rented. (2) Ijambo ry'imikorere 'for' mu buryo bwayo n'ijambo 'rent' kugira ngo vyerekane ko ikintu kirimo ubwoko: 'for rent' (igitero). (3) Ijambo 'available' (irimo ubwoko) kugira ngo vyerekane ko iduha irimo ubwoko. (4) Amazina yihuse zeretse zeretse: 'apartment' (iduha), 'flat' (iduha, igitero mu icyongereza cy'Ubuhindu), 'landlord' (umutegeri), 'tenant' (umutegwa), 'deposit' (ububiko), 'rent' (igitero kuri mwezi), 'lease' (ububiko bw'igitero). (5) Kugira ngo ubaze ku bindi bintu, ubone 'How much is the rent?' (Igitero ni cyinge?) n' 'Is it furnished?' (Ifite imikorere?). Ku buryo bwa kumenya, nibuka ko mu icyongereza amajambo y'igishushanyo yarimo hagati y'ijambo ry'ubwoko: 'a small apartment', si 'an apartment small'.

concept_examples.text: I want to rent an apartment near the city center.
concept_examples.translation: Nshaka gutegura iduha hafi y'akagari k'umujyi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒnt tə rent ən əˈpɑːrtmənt nɪr ðə ˈsɪti ˈsɛntər/

concept_examples.text: How much is the rent per month?
concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ mʌtʃ ɪz ðə rɛnt pər mʌnθ/

concept_examples.text: The apartment is available for rent.
The landlord requires a deposit of one month's rent.
concept_examples.translation: Umutegeri yishakiye ububiko bw'igitero kuri mwezi umwe.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈlændlɔrd rɪˈkwaɪərz ə dɪˈpɑzɪt əv wʌn mʌnθs rɛnt/

common_error.wrong: I need to rent a flat for center.
common_error.correct: I need to rent a flat near the center.
common_error.correct_alt: I need to rent a flat in the city center.
common_error.explanation: Ibikorwa by'ibibi ni kugira ubwoko 'for' ahandi 'near' cyangwa 'in' kugira ngo vyerekane aho. Mu igifaransa tubwira 'for the center' cyangwa 'by the center', nyamara mu icyongereza, 'for' bishobora kugirwa mu buryo bw'ubushakashatsi cyangwa ubufasha, si aho. Kugira ngo vyerekane ubwoko, tubona 'near' (hafi y') cyangwa 'in the city center' (mu akagari k'umujyi). Ihinda 'by' cyangwa 'for' ntibishobora guhindurwa mu buryo bw'ijambo ry'imikorere.

examples.original: apartment
examples.note: Mu icyongereza cy'Amerika, 'apartment' ni ikinyabiziga; mu icyongereza cy'Ubuhindu, 'flat' ni ikinyabiziga. Ebyiri byiza neza.

examples.original: rent (noun)
examples.note: Kugira ubwoko bw'ijambo, 'rent' ni amafaranga ufata kuri mwezi. Ntibishobora guhindurwa n'ijambo 'rent' (gutegura).

examples.original: landlord
examples.note: Mu icyongereza, 'landlady' ni umugore, nyamara 'landlord' bishobora kugirwa n'abantu bose.

examples.original: deposit
examples.note: Ni amafaranga ufata kugirango ubone ububiko. Hafi yaho, birahindurwa niba ntibifite ibibazo.

examples.original: How many bedrooms does the apartment have?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ ˈmɛni ˈbɛdrumz dʌz ðə əˈpɑːrtmənt hæv/
examples.note: Nibuka ko mu icyongereza, ibibazo by'uburenga 'how many' birangwa kuri ibintu byinshi (bedrooms).

examples.original: Is the rent included in the price?
examples.phonetic: /ɪz ðə rɛnt ɪnˈkludɪd ɪn ðə praɪs/
examples.note: Hano, 'rent' ni igitero kuri mwezi, kandi 'price' ni ikigereranyo cyangwa ububiko bw'ibinyabiziga.

examples.original: When can I move in?
examples.note: Ijambo 'move in' ni ukuvuga 'kwinjira mu iduha'.

examples.original: The apartment is furnished, but the kitchen is small.
examples.phonetic: /ðə əˈpɑːrtmənt ɪz ˈfɜːrnɪʃt bʌt ðə ˈkɪtʃən ɪz smɔl/
examples.translation: Iduha ifite imikorere, nyamara ikici cy'ukuboko ni kidogo.
examples.note: Bona 'but' (nyamara) kugira ngo vyerekane ibintu byiza n'ibibi.

examples.original: Can you lower the rent?
examples.note: Ijambo 'lower' ni ukuvuga 'kugura', hasi no mu bijyanye n'amafaranga.

examples.original: I'd like to sign a lease for one year.
examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk tə saɪn ə lis fɔr wʌn jɪr/
examples.translation: Nshaka kugura ububiko bw'igitero kuri mwaka umwe.
examples.note: Ijambo 'I'd like' ni ukuvuga 'I would like', kandi mu igifaransa ni ukuvuga 'nshaka'.

title: Making small talk at a party / Kuganira ibiganiro bishishana mu kwihuta
bridge: Mu igifaransa, iyo ubaza mu kwihuta, ubwenge nti ‘Comment ça va?’ cyangwa ‘Ça va?’ kandi tukoresha umubare ‘être’ kugena aho utuye. Mu icyongereza, tukoresha ‘How are you?’ ariko naho tukoresha ibintu nk’ ‘How’s it going?’ cyangwa ‘What’s up?’ bifite ubushishozi mu ibiganiro bishishana. Menya ko mu icyongereza, nta ‘I am agree’ (ibibazo by’ ingirakamaro), ahubwo ‘I agree’. Nanone, ibimenyetso ku byibazo nk’ ‘How are you?’ byarengera kuba bishishana no kuba bifite ubwoba, nk’ ‘I’m good, thanks’, naho ntibyo byiza cyane, mu kugaragaza ko mu igifaransa, ibintu byarengera kuba byinshi.
rule: Kugana ibiganiro bishishana mu kwihuta, koresha amahoro nk’ ‘Hey, how’s it going?’ cyangwa ‘What’s up?’ (ibimenyetso: ‘Not much, you?’). Kugana icyo ukeneye, vuga ‘I’m [name], nice to meet you’. Kugana icyo ukeneye, koresha ‘Would you like something to drink?’ (uburyo bw’ ubwoba) cyangwa ‘Do you want a drink?’ (bishishana). Kugana ibyo ukunda, koresha ‘I like...’ / ‘I don’t like...’. Kugana ubwoba, menya ko umubare ni ‘agree’ (nti ‘be agree’): ‘I agree with you’. Ibimenyetso ku byibazo nk’ ‘How are you?’ byarengera kuba by’ ubwoba: ‘I’m good’, ‘I’m fine’, ‘Pretty good’. Kugana ubwoba, koresha ‘It was nice talking to you’ cyangwa ‘See you later’.

concept_examples.text: Hi, I'm Maria. Nice to meet you.
concept_examples.phonetic: /haɪ aɪm məˈriːə naɪs tə miːt juː/

concept_examples.text: How's it going?
Would you like something to drink?
I agree with you, this party is great.
concept_examples.translation: Ndagiye n’ ubwawe, iyi si by’ ingirakamoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ əˈɡriː wɪð juː ðɪs ˈpɑːrti ɪz ɡreɪt/

common_error.explanation: Ibibazo byavuzwe kurema ‘estoy de acuerdo’ kugena aho utuye koresha umubare ‘to be’ (kuba). Mu icyongereza, ‘agree’ ni umubare w’ ingirakamoro, nta w’ ubwoba, bityo nta w’ ‘be’. Kugana ibyo ukeneye, menya ko ‘agree’ ni umubare w’ ‘do’ mu by’ ubwoba no mu byibazo: ‘I don’t agree’, ‘Do you agree?’.

examples.original: Hey, I'm John. What's your name?
examples.note: Koresha ‘What’s your name?’ kugana izina, ariko ni by’ ubushishozi kurusha ‘What is your name?’ mu ibiganiro bishishana.

examples.original: Nice to meet you, too.
examples.note: Koresha ‘too’ ku mwishyura kugana amahoro.

examples.original: This is my friend, Ana.
examples.note: Mu kwigana, ‘This is...’ ni by’ ingirakamoro kugana umunye.

examples.original: Can I get you a drink?
examples.note: ‘Can I...’ ni by’ ubushishozi no kuba by’ ingirakamoro. ‘May I...’ ni by’ ubwoba.

examples.original: Would you like some snacks?
examples.note: Koresha ‘some’ mu kugana, nta ‘any’.

examples.original: Could you pass me the chips, please?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː pæs miː ðə tʃɪps pliːz/
examples.translation: Wishimiye gutuma ibiryo by’ ubwoba, n’ ubwawe?
examples.note: ‘Could’ ni by’ ubwoba kurusha ‘can’ mu kushinsha.

examples.original: Wow, this is fun!
examples.note: Koresha ‘Wow’ kugena ubwoba.

examples.original: I really like this music.
examples.note: Shyiramo ‘really’ mbere y’ umubare kugena ubwoba.

examples.original: It was nice talking to you. See you later!
examples.phonetic: /ɪt wʌz naɪs ˈtɔːkɪŋ tə juː siː juː ˈleɪtər/
examples.translation: Byari by’ ubwoba kuganira n’ ubwawe. Tugeze mbere!
examples.note: Kugana ubwoba, koresha ‘It was nice talking to you’ maze ‘See you later’ kugana ubwoba.

examples.original: I have to go now. Thanks for having me!
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv tə ɡoʊ naʊ θæŋks fər hævɪŋ miː/
examples.translation: Nkeneye kuhagarika. Nshamiye kuba n’ ubwawe!
examples.note: Shukura umutegetsi n’ ‘Thanks for having me’.

title: Complaining and Apologizing / Kugirira ibyishimo no kuba impuhwe
bridge: Mu gaciri, ubwo ushaka kuba impuhwe, ubwokoze 'ndabibuka' cyangwa 'mbabibuka', ariko mu Icyongereza, harimo ibyerekana: 'I'm sorry' bishobora kuba bishoboye kurushwa mu kuba impuhwe byo hagati, kandi 'excuse me' bishobora kuba bishoboye kurushwa mu gutegura umuntu cyangwa mu kuba impuhwe byo bishishana. Nanone, mu byo kugirira ibyishimo, Icyongereza bishobora gusaba 'can't' cyangwa 'won't' mu kubwira ubwoba, kandi mu gaciri, ushobora kuvuga 'ntashobora' cyangwa 'ntishimiye' mu buryo bwa kuri. Kanga ubwoba n'uburyo bwo kwinjira 'to' nyuma yo kwandika 'sorry'.
rule: Mu kugirira ibyishimo mu Icyongereza, ushobora gushimisha 'I can't + verbo' (ntashobora) cyangwa 'This is + adjetivo' (ibi ni + adjetivo). Mu kuba impuhwe, ushobora gushimisha 'I'm sorry (for) + gerundio' cyangwa 'I apologize for + sustantivo'. Remera ko 'sorry' bishobora kwinjirira 'for' ubwo ubwira impamvu (I'm sorry for being late). Mu mibare yo mu burundu, 'I apologize' ni byo byoroshye kurushwa.

concept_examples.text: I'm sorry for being late.
This is really annoying.
I can't find my keys.
Excuse me, could you help me?

common_error.wrong: I am sorry, but I have a problem.
common_error.correct: I'm sorry, but I have a problem.
common_error.correct_alt: Excuse me, I have a problem.
common_error.explanation: Mu Icyongereza cyongereye, 'I'm' ni byo byoroshye kurushwa kurushwa 'I am' mu kwivugana. Kubw'ubwenge, 'I am' bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa mu mibare yo mu burundu. Nanone, mu gutangira kugirira ibyishimo mu buryo bw'umunyamuryango, abanyarwanda bashobora gushimisha 'I am sorry' naho batari mu kuba impuhwe, ariko mu Icyongereza, 'excuse me' ni byo byoroshye kurushwa mu gutegura umuntu mbere yo kugirira ibyishimo.

examples.original: I'm sorry.
examples.note: Bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa mu kuba impuhwe by'ubwoba. Mu gaciri, 'ndabibuka' ni byo byoroshye kurushwa, ariko mu Icyongereza, 'I'm sorry' ni byo byoroshye kurushwa.

examples.original: I apologize.
examples.note: Byoroshye kurushwa kurushwa 'I'm sorry'. Bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa mu mibare yo mu burundu cyangwa n'abantu batazwi.

examples.original: Sorry about that.
examples.note: By'umwanya n'ubwokoze. Bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa n'abanyuabandi cyangwa mu mibare yo mu nsuku.

examples.original: I can't stand the noise.
examples.note: 'Can't stand' ni igisubizo gishishana kugirira ibyishimo. Mu gaciri, ushobora kuvuga 'ntashobora kugumana n'ubwoba', kandi ni nk'ibyo.

examples.original: This is not what I ordered.
examples.note: Bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa mu mahanga cyangwa mu masoko. Gushimisha 'ordered' mu kubwira ubwoba bwawe.

examples.original: The service is too slow.
examples.note: 'Too + adjetivo' bishobora kuba nk'ubwoba bw'ubwoba, nk'ubwoba bw'ubwoba mu gaciri.

examples.original: I've been waiting for an hour.
examples.note: Gushimisha ubwoba bw'ubwoba bw'ubwoba bw'ubwoba. Mu gaciri, ushobora kuvuga 'najye nari njye nshize isaha'.

examples.original: It's okay.
examples.note: Igisubizo cy'umwanya kwinjira mu kuba impuhwe. Mu gaciri, ushobora kuvuga 'ni byiza' cyangwa 'nta cyaha'.

examples.original: No problem.
examples.note: Byoroshye kurushwa mu Icyongereza cy'Amerika. Nk'ubwoba bw'ubwoba mu gaciri.

examples.original: That's all right.
examples.note: Ikindi kigezo cy'ubwoba bw'ubwoba, ariko byoroshye kurushwa kurushwa. Mu gaciri, 'nta cyaha' ni nk'ibyo.

examples.original: Don't worry about it.
examples.note: Bishobora kuba byoroshye kurushwa mu gutegura umuntu waba impuhwe. Nk'ubwoba bw'ubwoba mu gaciri.

title: Describing your hometown / Kugena umujyi wawe cyangwa umudugudu wawe
bridge: Mu gacuku, kugena umujyi wawe cyangwa umudugudu wawe, ubirimo urubuga 'to be' kugena igitangaza (big, small, quiet) na 'there is/there are' kugena ibintu. Mu ikinyarwanda, uvuga 'ni ukubwa' cyangwa 'haraheze ahantu', ariko mu gacuku niba ukeneye 'there is' ni yo ushishikarira isura n'umwe, kandi 'there are' ni yo ushishikarira ibintu byinshi. Nanone, uburyo urangiza amagambo ni nyabwenge: mbere ni umusubirwa maze uburimbura, nk'uko bivugwa 'My city is big'. Abanyarwanda bashimishije guhuza 'there is/are' cyangwa gutega igitangaza nyuma y'igisubizo, nk'uko bivugwa 'the city big' ahandi 'the big city'.
rule:
Kugena umujyi wawe cyangwa umudugudu wawe mu gacuku ku murongo wa A2, ubirimo ibirimo bifatika:

1. **Umusubirwa + urubuga 'to be' (am/is/are) + igitangaza**: Kugena ibintu by'ingene. Umubare: 'My town is small.' (Umudugudu wanjye ni ukubye).
   - Na amabwiriza: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we are, they are.
   - Igitangaza kirimo mbere y'igisubizo igishishikarira: 'a big city', si 'a city big'.

2. **Haraheze / Harimo**: Kugena ko harimo ikintu kumujyi wawe.
   - Haraheze + igisubizo gisura/gishishikarira nta na rimwe: 'Haraheze ahantu.' (Haraheze ahantu).
   - Harimo + igisubizo gishishikarira ibintu byinshi: 'Harimo amashuri atandatu.' (Haraheze amashuri atandatu).
   - Mu gahinda: Nta na rimwe / Nta na rimwe: 'Nta kino kino.' (Nta kino).
   - Mu ibibazo: Haraheze...? Harimo...? (Haraheze...?).

3. **Imirimo y'ahantu**: Kugena ahantu y'ibintu.
   - 'mu gitegatsi' (mu gitegatsi), 'ku rutonde' (ku rutonde), 'hafi' (hafi y'), 'hafi y' (hafi y').

4. **Imirimo y'igikorwa**: 'Ungahanga', 'ungahura', 'haraheze' niyo yongeye kugena 'ungahura'.

5. **Imirimo y'urutonde**: Birimo 'and' kugena ibintu byinshi na 'but' kugena gutangira: 'Umudugudu wanjye ni ukubye ariko ni wiza.' (Umudugudu wanjye ni ukubye ariko ni wiza).

Kuri A2, gushishikarira amagambo yoroshye na yombanye. Niba ukeneye 'there is' ni yo ushishikarira ibintu byinshi – ntuvuge 'there is many shops'.

concept_examples.text: My city is big and modern.
concept_examples.translation: Umujyi wanjye ni ukubwa na modern.

concept_examples.text: There is a beautiful park in the center.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈbjuːtɪfʊl pɑːrk ɪn ðə ˈsentər/

concept_examples.text: There are two small shops near my house.
concept_examples.translation: Harimo amashuri atandatu hafi y'inyuma y'igikorwa cyanjye.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑː tuː smɔːl ʃɒps nɪər maɪ haʊs/

concept_examples.text: My town is quiet, but it's very friendly.
concept_examples.translation: Umudugudu wanjye ni uruhare, ariko ni wiza kandi ufite ubwoba.
concept_examples.phonetic: /maɪ taʊn ɪz ˈkwaɪət bʌt ɪts ˈveri ˈfrendli/

common_error.correct_alt: There is a church in my town.
common_error.explanation: Ibikorwa by'ingene ni ukubirimo 'have' na umuntu w'umwe (he/she/it). Mu gacuku, kuri 'town' (it) birimo 'has'. Nanone, abanyarwanda bashimishije kurema 'there is' na kubirimo 'have' nk'uko bivugwa 'umudugudu wanjye ufite igikorwa'. Mu gacuku, kugena ubutegetsi, ni byoroshye gusa 'there is' kurusha 'to have'.

examples.original: My city is very big.
examples.note: Birimo 'very' kugena kugira ububiko, nk'uko 'muyubye' mu ikinyarwanda.

examples.original: It is small and quiet.
examples.note: Niba ukeneye 'quiet' ni yo kugena ruhare (nta nshobora), si 'quite' (byinshi).

examples.original: The city is busy in the morning.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈsɪti ɪz ˈbɪzi ɪn ðə ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/
examples.note: Mu gacuku, kugena ibintu by'ingene byoroshye birimo 'is', ariko 'busy' bishobora kuba by'ingene; ahantu ni kugena uburyo bw'ingene.

levels.label: Describing places with 'there is' and 'there are'

examples.original: There is a museum and a library.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə mjuːˈziːəm ænd ə ˈlaɪbrəri/
examples.note: Iyo ubwira ibintu byinshi, birimo 'there is' kuri ya mbere cyangwa niba ni ibintu byinshi, ariko na ibintu byinshi birimo 'there are'.

examples.original: There are many restaurants in the main square.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑː ˈmeni ˈrestərɒnts ɪn ðə meɪn skweər/
examples.translation: Harimo amashuri menshi mu rugo rwa mbere.
examples.note: Birimo 'many' na ibintu byinshi byishishikarira, nk'uko 'amashuri menshi'.

examples.original: Is there a supermarket near here?
examples.note: Kugena ibibazo, gushishikarira: 'Is there...?'

examples.original: There aren't any museums in my town.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːnt ˈeni mjuːˈziːəmz ɪn maɪ taʊn/
examples.note: Birimo 'aren't any' kugena gutangira ibintu byinshi; 'there isn't' kuri ibintu bisura.

examples.original: I love my city because it's beautiful.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ lʌv maɪ ˈsɪti bɪkəz ɪts ˈbjuːtɪfʊl/
examples.translation: Nyakunde umujyi wanjye kubera ko ni wiza.
examples.note: Birimo 'because' kugena kugira ububiko, nk'uko 'kubera' mu ikinyarwanda.

examples.original: You should visit the old castle.
examples.note: Birimo 'should' kugena kugira ububiko; mu ikinyarwanda 'wibe'.

examples.original: It's a great place to live.
examples.note: 'A great place' ni kugena ahantu hagati; birimo 'live' (ubuzima) si 'in' mu mwishura.

translations.rw: Kugena umujyi wawe cyangwa umudugudu wawe

title: Talking About Hobbies / Kuganira iby’amahoro
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugana iby’amahoro tubona amagambo nk’agomba’ ‘gustar’ cyangwa ‘encantar’ hamwe n’ijambo rifite ububiko (‘me gusta’, ‘te gusta’), kandi akenshi tubwira tuti ‘me gusta + infinitivo’. Mu Icyongereza, ijambo ‘like’ rigira ubwoko bw’uburyo bwa kurema: ‘I like + -ing’ cyangwa ‘I like + to + ijambo’. Ubundi buryo bwo kugira ubwoko ni uko mu Icyongereza ntidufata amajambo yo mu minsi kandi mu masaha nk’uko tubwira tuti ‘on Mondays’ (los lunes), kandi mu gaciri akenshi tubwira tuti ‘los lunes’. Ubundi buryo, mu Icyongereza tubona ‘do’ kugira ngo tubaze iby’amahoro (‘What do you do in your free time?’), kandi mu gaciri tubwira tuti ‘¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?’.
rule: Kugana iby’amahoro mu Icyongereza (ububiko bw’A2): fata ijambo ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ cyangwa ‘prefer’ hamwe n’ijambo cyangwa ijambo rifite ububiko bwa -ing (ere. ‘I like music’, ‘I love playing soccer’). Ubundi buryo, fata ‘be interested in’ + ijambo cyangwa ububiko bwa -ing (ere. ‘I’m interested in photography’). Kugira ngo ubaze, fata ‘What do you like doing?’ cyangwa ‘What do you do in your free time?’. Kugira ngo ubaze ubwoko, fata amagambo nk’ ‘always’, ‘usually’, ‘sometimes’, ‘never’ mbere y’ijambo rifite ububiko bwa kurema (ere. ‘I usually read’). Ubundi buryo, fata amajambo yo mu biro nk’ ‘in’ (in my free time), ‘on’ (on weekends, on Mondays) na ‘at’ (at home, at the weekend – mu Icyongereza cy’Ubuvanganiza). Kwigomeka: ntidufata ‘do’ hamwe n’ ‘like’ mu masaha y’uburyo bwa kurema kugira ngo tubaze (tubwira tuti ‘I like’, si ‘I do like’ keretse kugira ngo tubaze neza).

concept_examples.text: I like listening to music.
She loves playing tennis.
What do you do in your free time?
concept_examples.translation: Uba ubyi bya kugura mu gihe cy’amahoro?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt duː juː duː ɪn jɔː friː taɪm/

concept_examples.text: I usually go hiking on weekends.
concept_examples.translation: Akenshi njya mu kwiyambukira mu mbere y’icyumweru.

common_error.explanation: Iyi ngororero igomba kubera ko mu gaciri tubwira tuti ‘me gusta jugar’ tubona infinitivo, kandi abanyamyuga bafata uburyo bwo gufata mu Icyongereza. Ndetse, mu Icyongereza, nyuma y’ ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ adi, tubona ububiko bwa -ing cyangwa infinitivo hamwe n’ ‘to’ (ariko ntibifite infinitivo bigoye ‘to’). Kugira ngo ubyitinke, remera: nyuma y’ ‘like’, fata ububiko bwa -ing: ‘I like playing’. Ubundi buryo, no fata ‘I like to play’, ariko ntibigomba.

examples.original: I love reading books.
examples.note: Fata ‘love’ + -ing kugira ngo ubaze ubwoko bw’uburyo bwa kugomba. Mu gaciri tubona ‘encantar’.

examples.original: She enjoys painting.
examples.note: ‘Enjoy’ byabanjirije n’ -ing. Ntibwira ‘enjoy to paint’.

examples.original: I don't like cooking.
examples.note: Kugira ngo ubye, fata ‘don’t’ + like + -ing. Mu gaciri: ‘no me gusta’.

examples.original: What do you like doing?
examples.note: Iyi ni uburyo bwa kubaza iby’amahoro. Mu gaciri: ‘¿Qué te gusta hacer?’

examples.original: Do you play any sports?
examples.note: Fata ‘play’ hamwe n’amashini yo mu biro (play football, play tennis). Mu gaciri: ‘jugar’.

examples.original: How often do you go to the cinema?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ ˈɒfən duː juː ɡəʊ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.translation: Uba ubyi byinshi ugura mu kino?
examples.note: Mu gaciri tubona ‘iraguha mu kino’ hamwe n’ ‘a’; mu Icyongereza tubona ‘go to + lugar’.

examples.original: I often watch TV in the evening.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɒfən wɒtʃ ˌtiːˈviː ɪn ðə ˈiːvnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Akenshi njya mu kureba tereve mu gice.
examples.note: Amagambo yo mu biro (often, usually, always) aha mbere y’ijambo rifite ububiko bwa kurema. Mu gaciri tubwira tuti ‘a menudo’.

examples.original: I prefer playing video games to reading.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ prɪˈfɜː ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈvɪdiəʊ ɡeɪmz tə ˈriːdɪŋ/
examples.translation: Ndagomba kugura amashini kurusha kumenya ibitabo.
examples.note: Kugira ngo ubaze ubwoko, fata ‘prefer A to B’, hamwe n’ububiko bwa -ing. Mu gaciri: ‘prefiero X a Y’.

examples.original: On Sundays, I usually go for a walk.
examples.phonetic: /ɒn ˈsʌndeɪz aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli ɡəʊ fər ə wɔːk/
examples.translation: Ku mbere y’icyumweru, akenshi njya mu kwiyambukira.
examples.note: Fata ‘on’ hamwe n’iminsi yo mu mbere y’icyumweru. Mu gaciri tubwira tuti ‘los domingos’.
